correctness.rationale: Each rank-one idempotent is the unique projector for an ordered pair of distinct image/kernel lines, hence corresponds bijectively to an oriented edge on q+1 vertices. A common invariant line forces a proper line-stabilizer algebra; without one, fixing the first projector as E11 yields separate nonzero E21 and E12 corner witnesses from the tuple and hence all four matrix units. For r>=1, an edge has exactly two endpoints, so exact inclusion-exclusion needs only one-point and two-point terms, giving the claimed count for all prime powers and all r>=1. The r=2 factorization and exceptional q=2, r=3 computation follow algebraically. Full tuple enumeration with independent matrix-span closure was run for q=2,3,4,5,7 at the explicitly listed tuple lengths; it corroborates but does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Targeted literature and semantic research searches on rank-one idempotent generating tuples, projective-line incidence and the characteristic-two three-projector threshold found no stated or logically dominating result. Petrenko–Sidki (2005) addresses unrestricted generating pairs; Sercombe–Shalev (2020) gives asymptotic fixed-characteristic-polynomial and fixed-rank probabilities, with neither the exact arbitrary-arity formula nor the binary triple boundary. Crestani (2012) addresses covering and pairwise generation; the accessible abstract and bibliographic record do not resolve whether the full paper contains an equivalent restricted enumeration, which remains an explicitly named originality risk.
residual_risks: Crestani 2012 full original text was unavailable; equivalent constrained tuple enumerations not ruled out there or in other unindexed literature.

The all-r formula is a natural complete invariant derived from elementary incidence counting; its mathematical value rests on exact constrained generation and the non-pairwise binary threshold, not on difficulty or paper-scale scope.

value.rationale: Exact probability of random generation under a natural severe constraint (nonzero rank-one idempotents), uniformly over all finite fields and every tuple length, addresses the restricted-generator question motivated by random associative-algebra generation. The line-incidence criterion is structural: it characterizes generation even when no pair generates, as over F2. The sharp minimal-arity jump (three at q=2 versus two otherwise) is not implied by generic two-element generation of M2; the complete all-arity law is usable for finite-field sampling and matrix-ring generation questions. This is not a claim to an unrelated downstream theorem or to computational novelty alone.
